proposition.claim:
For any feature map the solution has epsilon retrieval throughout each memory neighborhood, and the proposed normalized exponential feature map yields the prescribed dense/sparse Hopfield rule as the SVR optimizer.

The stated exponential upper bound uses the gap <xi_mu,x>-max_{nu!=mu}<xi_mu,xi_nu>.

Sparse retrieval error is no greater than dense retrieval error, which is used to support improved convergence and fixed-point conclusions.

A sufficient separation condition underlies the spherical-memory exponential-capacity derivation.

Released sparse retrieval implements the paper's normalization over the retained memory support.

repair.content:
Status: partial_precise_scope_only

Description: Restrict the constraint guarantee to sampled inputs and retain learned dual coefficients in the representer solution. No general neighborhood theorem or equality to prescribed softmax weights is certified.

Status: verified_for_explicit_subcase

Description: For noiseless keys/values, retained target and fixed mask, define g=<x,xi_mu>-max_{j retained,j!=mu}<x,xi_j> and q=(k-1)exp(-beta*g). Then ||T-xi_mu||<=2m q/(1+q)<=2m(k-1)exp(-beta*g); k=1 gives exact retrieval. The report supplies the complete probability-ratio and triangle-inequality proof.

Status: not_certified

Description: No universal sparse/dense error ordering is proposed. Specific configurations and independently justified fixed-support convergence remain possible.

Status: not_certified

Description: Mask excluded logits with negative infinity or normalize only selected original logits, retaining at least one item.
